items.finding: A presence rule with no keys routed '*' through the identifier quoter and compiled to SELECT [], COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY [] — valid to the guard but broken SQL, and no fixture covered it.
items.fix: fixed: a keyless presence rule now compiles a plain COUNT(*) with no GROUP BY, with a test asserting the statement and that no empty identifier appears

items.finding: Rule.type was a plain string, not narrowed to RULE_TYPES as the plan said.
items.fix: fixed: Rule.type is now RuleType, derived from RULE_TYPES

items.finding: custom-check returns a problem rather than carrying a referenced statement through, a departure from the plan that Progress did not record.
items.fix: answered: recorded in Progress; packs cannot carry SQL (ADR-0010), so the named-check registry belongs to the unit that first needs one

summary: All three ADRs are met by construction (parameterised scope values, strip()-guarded identifiers, exact six rule types, exact six cause words, 7-day/31-day windowing) and the kernel stays pure with no new dependencies or pack reads.
